name: Cloud TPU v3 ICI (inter-chip interconnect), 2D torus, 1024-chip pod
bandwidth_basis: NO PER-CHIP ICI BANDWIDTH IS PUBLISHED FOR v3, and none is inferred here. Google's v3 page publishes pod-level capacity and collectives only: TPU Pod size 1024 chips, all-reduce bandwidth per pod 340 TB/s, bisection bandwidth per pod 6.4 TB/s, peak compute per pod 126 PFLOPS bf16. It does not publish a per-chip ICI bandwidth, an ICI port count, or a link count - the 'interconnect topology 2D torus' row is the only interconnect detail on the page. The typed value is deliberately null rather than derived: 340 TB/s / 1024 chips would be a per-chip collective-rate artefact, not a link rate. v3 is recorded because it is the last generation before v4's optical 3D mesh, and because its 53:1 all-reduce-to-bisection ratio is the baseline the later 2D generations (v5e, v6e at 32:1) improve on.
topology: 2D TORUS across a 1024-chip pod, published as 'Interconnect topology: 2D torus'. Pod-level collectives as documented: all-reduce bandwidth per pod 340 TB/s against bisection bandwidth per pod 6.4 TB/s, a ratio of about 53. This is the same shape of result as v5e and v6e but worse, and it is the clearest illustration in this set that the all-reduce-to-bisection ratio is a property of the 2D torus rather than of the bandwidth: raising per-chip bandwidth on a torus does not change the ratio, and only leaving the 2D torus (v4's 3D mesh/torus, ~46:1, then v5p's 3D torus) changes it. Note that v3's published page does NOT mention twisted topologies - Google documents those for v4 and v5p only.
switching: ICI is the scale-up fabric and the scale-up domain is the 1024-chip POD. Google's documented boundary is ICI versus DCN, not 'scale-up'/'scale-out': ICI is 'high speed, low latency internal links that connect TPUs within a TPU Pod'; cross-slice traffic goes 'by transferring data to CPUs (hosts) which in turn transmit the data over the data-center network (DCN)', 'a higher latency, lower-throughput network (when compared with ICI)'. The booleans are this repo's mapping of that boundary. SCALE-OUT: the v3 page publishes NO per-host NIC configuration and NO DCN bandwidth figure of any kind, so nothing is recorded - v3 predates the v5-generation pod-level DCN figures in this set and this is a genuine documentation gap rather than an omission. Google's v3 page also predates the Multislice product surface (the Multislice Overview's accelerator-type definition begins at 'a TPU type (v4 or later)'), so the documented way to exceed one pod on v3 is not covered by any source in this record set.
notes: Included for the torus ratio and for completeness of the ICI lineage, not because anyone provisions it - the v3 page lists supported accelerator types v3-8 through v3-2048 with 'Support ends' set to '(End date not yet set)' for every row, which is itself the useful fact: Google has published no end-of-support date for v3. SLICE NAMING TRAP, SAME SHAPE AS v4: v3 slice names are TensorCore-based, so v3-8 is 4 chips and v3-2048 is 1024 chips - reading the trailing number as a chip count overstates by 2x. HOST PACKING IS NOT PUBLISHED for v3: the page has no 'chips per host' row, so the number of hosts in a 1024-chip pod is not derivable from this source and is not recorded. The 32-GiB HBM2 per chip at 900 GBps is on the v3 page but is a memory figure, not an interconnect one. Sources: cloud-tpu-v3-system-architecture for every figure on this record; w7c-google-tpu-multislice-overview for the ICI/DCN definitions and for the fact that Multislice accelerator types are defined from v4 onward.
